Autumn Jazz Ticket Bundle: Swing into Fall for only $90 with our Autumn Jazz Package. From the vibrant Brazilian rhythms and dazzling musicianship of Jovino Santos Neto, to the celebrated jazz and chamber ensembles of the Brian Dickinson Trio with the Penderecki String Quartet, and the swinging big-band tradition of Jim Galloway’s Wee Big Band, experience all that jazz has to offer. 

Three-time Latin Grammy nominee Jovino Santos Neto, a master pianist, composer and arranger, is one of the most important Brazilian musicians working today. Currently based in Seattle, Washington, he has throughout his career been closely affiliated with the Brazilian master Hermeto Pascoal. He was an integral part of Pascoal's group from 1977 to1992 where he fine-tuned his artistry, performing around the world and co-producing several legendary records. Pascoal, who passed away last year at age 89, was described by the Guardian as a "brilliant multi-instrumentalist and composer who beguiled the world with fusions of north-Brazilian rural music, jazz and contemporary-classical forms, and mimicry of all manner of forest and city sounds. If ever a contemporary musician deserved to be called a force of nature, it was Pascoal."

Jovino’s personal style is a creative blend of energetic grooves, deep harmonies, telepathic improvisation, lyrical melodies and great ensemble playing, always inspired and informed by the colorful richness of Brazilian music. His compositions include samba, choro, baião, xote, forró, marcha and many more styles, rooted in centuries-old musical tradition while pointing to new and adventurous harmonic languages. Jovino currently leads his Seattle-based Quinteto and Trio. He taught piano and composition at Cornish College of the Arts for 26 years. He can also be heard around the world as a piano soloist, working with symphony orchestras, jazz big bands, chamber music groups, and in collaboration with musicians such as his mentor Hermeto Pascoal, Bill Frisell, Paquito d’Rivera, Airto Moreira, Claudio Roditi, David Sanchez, Joe Locke, Anat Cohen and many more.

This unique concert will pay tribute to Hermeto and Jovino's music, with Mark Kelso (drums), Roberto Occhipinti (bass), Michael Occhipinti (guitar), and Christine Jensen (woodwinds). Thursday September 17.

Alma/Universal recording artist Micah Barnes salutes Montreal’s favourite son in an intimate concert of Leonard Cohen classics! Micah’s rich baritone voice brings a new perspective to Leonard Cohen’s powerful lyrics, honouring the intricacy of the storytelling and the depth of musicality in these much-celebrated songs. Join Micah and his band of top-flight musicians, including guest vocalist Rique Franks, on a magical journey though Leonard’s world! Friday September 18.

Opening set by  Barbara Lynch is one of those special artists whose music not only happily spans categories, but also time and place. In her music you can hear echoes of jazz, folk, blues, barrel-house boogie and old-time religion hymns. It wouldn't be out of place in the New Orleans of the early 1990's. The south side of Chicago in the 1950's, 52nd street in its' heyday, or the West Coast of the 1970's. In other words, she is a genuine 21 st century artist. She would be an excellent addition to any music bill.

“Mysticssippi” bluesman Harry Manx has been called an “essential link” between the music of East and West, creating musical short stories that wed the tradition of the blues with the depth of classical Indian ragas. He has created a unique sound that is hard to forget and deliciously addictive.

Harry forged his distinctive style by studying at the feet of the masters, first as a sound man in the blues clubs of Toronto during his formative years, and then under a rigorous tutelage with Vishwa Mohan Bhatt in India. Bhatt is the inventor of the 20-stringed Mohan Veena, which has become Harry’s signature instrument.

Harry played slide guitar for many years before meeting Bhatt in Rajasthan. He started at the beginning under Bhatt’s tutelage, unlearning most of what he knew about playing a slide instrument. He learned Eastern scales and eventually ragas, deceptively complex and regimented musical patterns that form the basis of Indian composition. Learning the voicings of Indian music is a subtle art that comes with time. Harry spent most of twelve years in India learning that. It was later that Harry decided to explore the connection between Indian ragas and blues scales which eventually led to the Indo-blues hybrid that has become his style. Saturday September 19.

Joining Harry will be Clayton Doley from Australia on Hammond organ, Kevin Breit on guitar and Steve Marriner on bass and harmonica. They will be playing songs from Harry's new release Falling Upwards.

Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm
$15+ in advance, $22+at the door

Dynesti (she/her)

Toronto songwriter, singer, rapper, dancer, and powerhouse performer Dynesti can transform any space with a potent mix of raw honesty, life lessons, humour, and collective participation. Blending neo-soul and conscious hip-hop with splashes of reggae, dancehall and afrofusion, her infectious vibe motivates people to unleash their authentic selves through bold expression. She rose from the shelter system and programs like SKETCH Working Arts, RISE Edutainment, The Remix Project, and Honey Jam to share stages with stars like Sean Paul and Talib Kweli. Her gutsy 2027 album ‘The Dyna: Breakfast’ speaks on womanhood, community, wellness, love, and relationships as a Black girl from a broken home. 

J3M (he/him)

J3M combines pop, disco, and soul into an infectious sound that will stay with you long after the show is over. A singer, songwriter, producer, instrumentalist and uplifting performer, he was a 3rd Prize Winner in Canada’s Walk of Fame 2023 RBC Emerging Musician Program and has appeared at Pride festivals nationwide, Casa Loma, River & Sky Festival, and much more. He’s a 2026 Capital Music Award nominee and has been featured on JUNO- and Polaris-nominated releases as a keyboardist. J3M has shared stages with artists including Jully Black and Cyndi Lauper, and backed artists such as Yukon Blonde, Tanika Charles, Zaki Ibrahim, Lu Kala, and The OBGMs across Canada and internationally. His latest single ‘Love Addict’ is available everywhere.

Grace Marr (she/her)

Grace Marr, is a Canadian powerhouse vocalist and multi-genre songwriter with a knack for weaving depth into pop hooks, gospel-inspired harmonies, and a gritty demeanour. Already achieving notoriety for her independently-released debut album, ‘Saving Grace’ (Top 5 Canadian Christian Radio CANCON, Spotify Editorial Playlists), Grace can be seen on stages such as RBC Bluesfest Emerging Showcase, Breakfast Television, and singing the anthem for WNBA Toronto Tempo games. As a Queer singer-songwriter and avid sports fan, Marr recently nodded to women's achievement in sports and her hockey crush in her Toronto Sceptres-inspired single, ‘Take A Shot On Me’. 

Folke (they/them)

Folke is a multi-instrumentalist (guitar, violin, viola, cello, harp, saxophone) and intuitive composer born in New Jersey and based for many years in Canada. They bring folk & soul roots with a melody of strings that move like wind; gentle, directional, and impossible to ignore. The storytelling grit of Tracy Chapman combines with the structural precision of Bach into a sound that feels both timeless and restless. Already a fixture in Toronto's experimental and folk-adjacent scenes, they are building a catalog that bridges folk intimacy with soulful expansiveness and recording a debut solo album.

Nefe (they/them)

Enshrined within Nefe’s rock and soul sensibilities you find an artist who is equal parts songwriting oracle and vocal magician. Masterfully in control of their sonant undulations, combined with lyrical rawness, their songs lure listeners into a journey through a rich musical tapestry built upon the frame of alternative soul and R&B.

results.description:
Mother Country presents The Sign of Jonas in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue

Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm
$25+ in advance, $32+at the door

Mother Country is here to chronicle the eternal journey home.

Their songs carry the grit of Southern folk, the sweep of Americana, and the reflective depth of someone who’s lived a thousand miles of road. The sound pulls from a wide range of roots: the storytelling of The Band, the cinematic scope of Iron & Wine, the exploratory edge of cosmic country.

The band is founded by Benton Roark, whose songs have been described as “backwoods-choir elegance” (The Georgia Straight) and “an experience of deep and darkling beauty” (The Austin Chronicle). Since leaving his hometown of Atlanta, GA (where early efforts dubbed him “a crafty folk-experimentalist,” Creative Loafing), Roark has called Ohio, NYC, Vancouver, St. John’s, Newfoundland, and Toronto home. He’s been a bandleader for a number of groups, the last of which was Rollaway, whose last two records - Modern Epic and The Return of the Lonesome Coyote Patchwork Pulpit (“tone poems in the style of My Morning Jacket,” Maverick Magazine) set the scene for Mother Country’s inception.

Taking up the Americana and Southern gothic mantle, and weaving it with the distinct threads of old time, bluegrass, and trad folk music, as well as the visionary poetry of Maritimes poet Luke Hathaway, Mother Country set out in late 2024 with its debut record, The Sign of Jonas (Milltown Records). An apocalypse folk-tale and concept album, the Jonas song cycle has been presented by English Harbour Arts, 10C Guelph, Camber Arts, Bannerman Brewing, and Halifax Central Library, and spent a number of weeks in the top ten Earshot radio charts in its first few months of existence. Thursday September 24.

An apocalypse folk-tale and concept album, the Jonas song cycle has been presented by English Harbour Arts, 10C Guelph, Camber Arts, Bannerman Brewing, and Halifax Central Library, and spent a number of weeks in the top ten Earshot radio charts in its first few months of existence. Jeff Madden - Sinatra In Love

Sinatra in Love is a romantic new cabaret celebrating the timeless songs of Frank Sinatra by award-winning actor/singer Jeff Madden. You’ll be swept away by nostalgia, heartfelt story-telling and the unforgettable melodies that made Sinatra an icon. With his rich vocals, effortless charm and acclaimed storytelling, Jeff takes audiences on a moving musical journey through every stage of love, from first glance and flirtation to passion, heartbreak and new beginnings. Featuring Sinatra's most beloved classics alongside rare musical gems, Sinatra in Love is an elegant, stylish and deeply entertaining evening that proves why these timeless songs continue to resonate across generations.

About the Artist:

Jeff Madden is a Toronto-based singer, actor and educator, and a leading member of this country’s musical theatre scene. An original Canadian cast member of Mirvish’s Come From Away, Jeff performed the role of “Kevin T & others” more than 700 times between 2018-2025. He also played “Claude and others” in the Gander, Newfoundland production of that show. Jeff is best known as Canada’s first “Frankie Valli”, starring in the Canadian premiere of Jersey Boys, winning the coveted Dora Award for Outstanding Performance in a Musica’. Jeff performed that vocally grueling role 700 times in Toronto and across Australia between 2008-2013. He has recently created a dynamic show with Adrian Marchuk, called How We Got To Jersey - A Tale Of Two Frankies, which has delighted audiences across Ontario, and will play the Theatre Orangeville this September 25-27. 

Other Toronto theatre appearances include Shrek, Rock of Ages, Forever Plaid, Echoes, and I Love You Because (Dora Nomination). Elsewhere, Jeff played the lead role of Lawrence Jameson in Dirty Rotten Scoundrels in BC and appeared at the prestigious Shaw Festival for eight consecutive seasons, playing roles in Wonderful Town, Tristan, Belle Moral, Happy End, Floyd Collins and many more.

Jeff has appeared on TV’s Terminal List, Murdoch Mysteries, Mayday, Accused and The Parker-Andersons, recorded voice-over work, created a series of cabaret shows called “My Life In Song”, and recorded two CDs of musical theatre and pop songs. Jeff is a competent piano and trumpet player, holds a Master of Education degree from U of T, and teaches acting and singing privately in addition to being a part-time faculty member at Sheridan and Randolph Colleges off and on for many years. See him live at Hugh’s Room on Monday September 28.

Autumn Jazz Ticket Bundle: Swing into Fall for only $90 with our Autumn Jazz Package. From the vibrant Brazilian rhythms and dazzling musicianship of Jovino Santos Neto, to the celebrated jazz and chamber ensembles of the Brian Dickinson Trio with the Penderecki String Quartet, and the swinging big-band tradition of Jim Galloway’s Wee Big Band, experience all that jazz has to offer. 

Now celebrating its 46th year, the 16-piece Jim Galloway’s Wee Big Band proudly makes its first appearance at Hugh’s Room under the leadership and musical direction of early band member Brigham Phillips on piano. Formed in 1979 as a repertory band specializing in the music of the great bands of the swing era, Jim Galloway's Wee Big Band has over 400 arrangements, which is perhaps the most extensive repertoire of any big band in the country. The music of Duke Ellington has always been an integral part of the band's library, with examples of his work ranging from his early compositions in the late 20s to his sacred music in the 70s. Tributes to the bands of Count Basie, Benny Goodman, Woody Herman, Jimmie Lunceford, Jay McShann, Buddy Rich and Artie Shaw are also in the library.

From its very first engagement, a broadcast on CJRT-FM from the Ontario Science Centre, the band has made numerous radio broadcasts and television appearances and has played throughout Canada. Today, Jim Galloway’s Wee Big Band continues to perform at local jazz festivals, special occasion events, annual fundraisers and ongoing concerts at downtown jazz venues.

Leader Brigham Phillips, from Halifax, has been a professional musician since 1975 and has been based in Toronto since 1971. During this time, he has had the opportunity to work in most areas of the music business as a performer, band leader, musical director, contractor, arranger, composer and teacher/clinician. Brigham’s strength is his versatility. He plays piano, keyboards, trumpet, valve trombone and euphonium, sings and plays many styles of music – jazz, blues, big band/dance band, solo/cocktail piano, pop, light orchestra, Dixieland, musical theatre (Mirvish and Drayton), as well as composing and arranging in these styles. Friday October 2.

What if music is more than something we make, perform or listen to?
What if it can also help us heal?

On Monday October 5th Hugh's Room Live hosts MUSIC AS MEDICINE, bringing artists and community members together for an evening exploring the relationship between creativity, music and mental wellbeing. Part three of the series 'Let's Talk Burnout', the evening will begin with a live musical performance by Mimi O'Bonsawin, followed by a panel discussion and audience Q&A and will close with an informal opportunity to connect and continue the conversation with artists, panelists and fellow members of the community.

The evening will be led by singer-songwriter, filmmaker and educator Andrea Ramolo, whose documentary The South explores the traditional music, dance and healing rituals of Salento in southern Italy, where there are traditions that see music and dance as powerful tools for healing and community.

Andrea will moderate a conversation with artists/panelists about the ways creativity can support us through difficult times, and the different ways music be used as and around healing and medicine. The panel will also consider the balance between creating for ourselves and creating as a profession. How can we maintain a creative practice without allowing the pressures of the music industry to turn something restorative into another source of burnout?

This is a free event, and registration is encouraged to ensure your spot for this special evening. 

Presented by Revelios, Hugh’s Room and Creative Arts Financial

Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm
$40+ in advance, $47+ at the door

Conjuring a unique but universal language from that most ubiquitous of instruments, the acoustic guitar, Tony McManus has both extended and transcended the parameters of contemporary Celtic music. Ranked by peers and predecessors alike alongside the guitar world’s all-time greats, his fiendishly dexterous, dazzlingly original playing draws on traditions from the entire Celtic diaspora – Scotland, Ireland, Brittany, Galicia, Asturias, Cape Breton, and Quebec – along with still further-ranging flavours, such as jazz and east European music. Long applauded for his uncanny ability to transpose the delicate, complex ornamentation characteristic of traditional bagpipe or fiddle tunes – even the phrasing of a Gaelic song – onto his own six strings, McManus is increasingly being acknowledged also as a pioneering figure in bridging the realms of Celtic music and other guitar genres.

Joining Tony is John McMillan; an award-winning solo acoustic guitarist and composer best known for his atmospheric, instrumental music. Listening to John play live is like watching someone paint with sound. He weaves intricate emotions, shifting moods and even subtle shades of colour into song structures that feel deceptively simple, achieving a remarkable sense of effortlessness. John achieves wide tonal variety in his work, due in part to his use of a number of instruments, including the harp, tenor and baritone guitars, mandolin, dobro and Spanish laud.

Thursday October 8.

Stevie Wonder Songs in the Key of Life Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue

Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm
$40+ in advance, $47+at the door

Join us as we celebrate the 50th Anniversary of one of the greatest albums of all time, Stevie Wonder's Songs in The Key Of Life! Musical director Michael Occhipinti and members of the band Soul Stew will provide the backing as these great musicians put their own stamp on Stevie's iconic music. 

Featuring:

John Johnson/Saxophone 
David Gray/Guitar 
Matt Horner/Keyboards 
Mark Kelso/Drums (Austin Gembora subbing in) 
Roberto Occhipinti /Bass

Michael Dunston

Michael Dunston has spent decades entertaining internationally with sold out shows in Canada, the United States, The Hague and Australia. Michael has produced music that has been released worldwide and has written four songs for the upcoming movie Loanshark. He’s also had principal roles in Death Wish, Tommy Boy and most recently The Boys. Michael was crowned the jingle king in Canada in connection with the countless commercials he has sung. 

APHROSE 

Aphrose is a rising force in Canada’s soul/R&B scene, earning a 2025 JUNO Award nomination for Adult Contemporary Album of the Year for her critically acclaimed sophomore release, Roses. She is featured on the 2026 GRAMMY Award-winning album Immersed by Justin Gray and became a Recording Academy (GRAMMY) and CARAS (JUNO) voting member in 2025. Blending R&B and Neo-Soul with vintage warmth and a modern edge, she creates timeless, emotionally resonant music that continues to captivate audiences at home and abroad. 

Lester McLean 

Lester McLean is one of Toronto’s most dynamic frontmen, a powerful lead vocalist, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist who plays saxophone, guitar and percussion. His unique soulful sound draws equally on the funk and soul of artists like Stevie Wonder and his love of acoustic songwriters such as Neil Young. The result is an artist who can take an audience from an intimate acoustic whisper to a full-on electric funk jam. Lester has released three albums under his own name, Best Foot Forward, LM 4,3,2,1, and A Mostly A Capella Christmas. Lester was a member of the funk-fusion band Colour of Soul, and is the long-time lead vocalist for Toronto party band Grooveyard. He has performed with Maestro, Jacksoul, Trey Anastasio, Colin James, Divine Brown, Ron Sexsmith, Dan Hill, and Jim Cuddy. 

Soul Stew featuring Michael Dunston

Formed in 1990 by Toronto first call studio musicians as a house band at the Bamboo, Soul Stew became the band synonymous with the College Street music scene with their 10-year long residency at the College Street bar. The musicians in Soul Stew have collectively and individually performed and recorded with The Boss Brass, Gorillaz, Bruce Cockburn, Paul Butterfield, The Parachute Club, Holly Cole, Gino Vanelli, Tito Puente, Aretha Franklin and Nelly Furtado, to name just a few. Soul Stew plays a mixture of blues, jazz, rhythm and blues, funk, a bit of reggae and a lot of soul, recalling the classic sounds of the legendary recording bands (a la the Funk Brothers from the movie Standing in the Shadows of Motown) of Stax, Motown, The Philly Sound, Muscle Shoals, and the Hi Rhythm section of Memphis. 

Ammoye
Ammoye's music is a fusion of reggae, dancehall, and R&B, delivering powerful vocals and meaningful lyrics that explore love, empowerment, and social justice. Join the movement of positive vibes and infectious beats as she seamlessly blends tradition with a modern global flair.

Hugh’s Goes Classical with Ryan Huang in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue
Curated by Eric Friesen and Angela Hewitt

Ryan Huang, 15, is one of Canada's leading young pianists. He is internationally recognized as a Young Steinway Artist and a Young Scholar of the Lang Lang International Music Foundation. In 2026, he became the first Canadian pianist to win First Prize and the Audience Prize at the prestigious Cleveland International Piano Competition for Young Artists (Junior Division). The same year, he was named one of CBC Music's 30 Hot Canadian Classical Musicians Under 30.

Ryan has been selected for several of North America's premier young artist programs, including the Morningside Music Bridge Program, the Aspen Music Festival and School, and, beginning in Fall 2026, the Pre-College Division of The Juilliard School in NYC.

A laureate of numerous international competitions, Ryan has received top prizes at the Nutcracker International Television Music Competition (Russia), the Fryderyk Chopin Piano Competition for Children and Youth (Poland), the Jeune Chopin Competition (Switzerland), the Kaufman International Youth Piano Competition (United States), the Euregio Piano Award (Germany), as well as the Canadian Music Competition and the Steinway Junior Piano Competition in Canada.

Ryan made his debut at Carnegie Hall's Stern Auditorium at the age of seven and gave his first solo recital at the Shanghai Symphony Hall at age eight. Since then, he has appeared as soloist with orchestras including the Toronto Symphony Orchestra, Moscow Philharmonic Orchestra, Wuhan Philharmonic Orchestra, Vienna Opera Ball Orchestra, Newfoundland Symphony Orchestra, Canton Symphony Orchestra, Vidin Symphony Orchestra, Oakville Symphony Orchestra, and Oakville Chamber Orchestra, North York Concert Orchestra, Burlington New Millenium Symphony Orchestra Cathedral Bluffs Symphony Orchestra, addition to orchestras throughout Italy and Poland.

In 2025, Ryan was invited by Lang Lang to perform an encore at the Toronto Symphony Orchestra's 30th Anniversary Concert at Roy Thomson Hall, where he received a standing ovation. As a Young Scholar of the Lang Lang International Music Foundation, he has also performed at international events, including a special concert on the Great Wall of China, after which he was named a Great Wall Young Ambassador. In 2026, the Town of Oakville recognized his artistic achievements and community contributions by naming him Oakville's Music Ambassador.

Ryan is an alumnus of the Phil and Eli Taylor Performance Academy for Young Artists. He currently studies with Dr. Michael Berkovsky, receives additional guidance and mentorship from Dr. Marilyn Engle, and studied with Dr. Olga Chichova during his formative years.

Beyond the concert stage, Ryan is a passionate volunteer who performs regularly for charity and teaches music to primary school students weekly. He remains dedicated to the philosophy that every child deserves the opportunity to explore the beauty of music and musical instruments.

Hugh’s Goes Classical Series in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue
Curated by Eric Friesen and Angela Hewitt


Hugh’s Room Goes Classical is the brainchild of Board member, Barbara Jesson, who invited pianist Angela Hewitt and broadcaster and speaker, Eric Friesen, to curate a first classical season for the Room.
After Angela played Hugh’s Room for the first time, in December 2024, she and Eric were inspired by the intimacy and acoustic excellence of the Room, and quickly imagined their first season.

Angela and Eric felt the Room must showcase major classical artists, like Angela herself and baritone Brett Polegato, in an up-close-and-personal format, rarely experienced by the audience for artists of that calibre.

Hugh’s Room is perfect for a more informal style of presentation, hosted by Eric Friesen, with the artists speaking briefly but effectively about their programs and themselves. They also felt it was a perfect venue and style of performance for emerging Canadian artists, like pianist Carter Johnson, first Canadian finalist at the Van Cliburn Competition, and mentored by Angela, to be introduced to a Toronto audience.

The same for the teenage phenomenon from Oakville, Ryan Huang, already a Lang Lang International Music Foundation Young Scholar and Young Steinway Artist. And finally, for the season ender, the brother/sister Cheng² Duo – cellist Bryan Cheng and pianist Silvie Cheng, who already have stellar international careers.


Sunday, Oct 18 2026 Ryan Huang -2pm
Sunday, Nov 22 2026 Brett Polegato and Robert Kortgaard
Sunday, Feb 7 2027 Cheng2 Duo - 2pm

Discoveries Vol. 14 with Musical Host Aleksi Campagne Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue

Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm
$15+ in advance, $20+at the door

Named Penguin Eggs & Roots Music Canada's New Discovery of the Year! , Aleksi Campagne offers a contemporary, indie-folk take on the time-honoured fiddle-singing tradition. Born and raised in Montreal, Aleksi’s music blends folk songwriting with an edgy, multi-layered sound resulting from his unique combination of voice, violin and looping-effect pedals. Aleksi was awarded the Canadian Folk Music Award for francophone artist of the year for his debut album in April 2024

Claire Turnbull is a flutist and singer-songwriter from the Eastern Townships of Quebec, where the region’s rich Irish, French Canadian and Scottish cultural heritage inspire her music. A dynamic performer, she has been playing the flute since the age of two and has built a versatile career spanning classical, folk and traditional music, all with the distinctive voice of her silver flute. Alongside guitarist and collaborator, Zach Bachand, her performances feature arrangements of traditional, Irish, Scottish and French tunes and original songs, blending her classical training with the rich storytelling traditions of folk and trad music. She has studied with internationally renowned flutists, notably James Galway and William Bennett. She holds a Bachelor of Music from McGill University and completed graduate studies at the Université de Montreal and the Longy School of Music. Claire has performed with orchestras, chamber ensembles, and bands, appearing at festivals and concert series across Canada, including a recent appearance as a featured soloist with Orchestre Fidelio.

Ryan Young is a Scottish fiddle player working within the traditional music of Scotland. His playing is noted for its distinctive tone and phrasing, with an approach that places melody and expression at the centre of the music. He first came to wider attention with his debut album, produced by four-time GRAMMY winner Jesse Lewis (Béla Fleck, Yo-Yo Ma), establishing the foundations of a career that has since developed an international reach. He has toured extensively across the UK, Europe, North America and Australia, and is recognised for a style that draws on both Scottish and Irish traditions.

Young is a multi award-winning artist and has received multiple nominations at the MG Alba Scots Trad Music Awards, including back-to-back nominations in recent years and most recently for Musician of the Year in 2025. He has also been a finalist in both the BBC Radio 2 Young Folk Awards and the BBC Radio Scotland Young Traditional Musician of the Year.

His recordings have received consistent critical attention, with The Scotsman awarding five-star reviews across his work. In live performance, he has been described as “a force of nature.”

Young’s third studio album, due for release in May 2026, is produced by and features Martin Hayes. Recorded with engineer Patrick Phillips (The Gloaming, Peter Gabriel), the album includes contributions from Stuart McCallum (The Breath, Cinematic Orchestra) and Louis Campbell (Sam Lee, Sam Sweeney).

“It’s not likely that you’ll ever hear the harmonica played so well and in so many different ways than at the hands of Cuban-born Torontonian Carlos del Junco.” John Terauds – TORONTO STAR

"A model of focus and urgency...a true virtuoso" - The Globe and Mail

"One listen to the man who bent his first notes on a harmonica at the age of 14 and it’s obvious he’s in a class with such greats as Toots Thielemans, Paul Butterfield and Howard Levy of Bela Fleck’s Flecktones.” - Edmonton Journal

Carlos del Junco has toured many parts of the globe and is considered one the world’s top diatonic harmonica players. He’s released ten recordings and is a dynamic live performer, having played virtually every major blues, folk and jazz festival in Canada. In addition to two JUNO nominations, del Junco won two gold medals for both blues and jazz categories at the Hohner World Harmonica Championships in 1993 in Germany. Playing a ten hole diatonic harmonica, Carlos has developed the unique ability to play chromatically by using an "overblow" technique. 

He’s one of the few pioneers of this overblow method, bringing musical credibility to what has still been considered by many in the music industry to be a fringe folk instrument. Get ready to trash all you thought about the harmonica as Carlos del Junco and The Blues Mongrels deliver a no holds barred display of melodic fun and virtuosity. Saturday October 24.

Maggie’s Wake is a dynamic and refreshing band from Southwestern Ontario, Canada, blending the timeless roots of traditional folk with the energy of varied music styles, including jazz, Americana, and classic country. Drawing on their heritage while forging new ground, their sound is both deeply rooted and wholly original. With a passion for celebrating the rich history of folk music in a modern voice, Maggie’s Wake seeks to inspire, uplift, and bring joy to audiences everywhere.

At the heart of the band are two award-winning musical powerhouses: songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Tara Dunphy (The Rizdales, Luther Wright and the Wrongs), whose soulful lead vocals and mastery of tin whistle, flute, and fiddle shine through every performance, and Lindsay Schindler (Rant Maggie Rant, Trent Severn), an internationally recognized fiddler, composer and author whose artistry is known for entrancing audiences. Together, they create a harmony-rich interplay that is the band’s signature. Rounding out the lineup is a group of equally celebrated musicians: Andrew Kosty on upright and electric bass, and Ken Palmer on acoustic and electric guitar. 

Since their debut, Maggie’s Wake has lit up sold-out theatres and concert halls, steadily building anticipation for their self-titled debut album, Maggie's Wake, which was released worldwide on March 17, 2024, to critical acclaim. Their artistry has also been recognized with multiple awards, including a Canadian Folk Music Award for Best New/Emerging Artist which they proudly accepted in April 2025.

​With their passion, precision, and originality, Maggie’s Wake continues to carve out an inspiring space in the contemporary folk music landscape. Sunday October 25.

Marshall Crenshaw with special guests Sarah Borges and Eric Ambel Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue

Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm
$50+ in advance, $60+at the door

Born in 1953 in Detroit, Michigan, Marshall Crenshaw learned to tune a guitar correctly at age ten and has been trying ever since. His first big break came in 1978 playing John Lennon in “Beatlemania”, first as an understudy in New York, then in the West Coast company, followed by a national touring company. Removing himself from that situation in Feb. 1980, Marshall settled in New York City. Enthralled by the hyper-diverse musical culture of the City, and the local Rock scene in particular, Marshall formed a Rock and Roll band with brother Robert on drums and Chris Donato on bass.

After crossing paths with the great and legendary Alan Betrock, Marshall recorded his debut single “Something’s Gonna Happen” for Betrock’s Shake Records label; at nearly the same time, legendary Rockabilly singer Robert Gordon’s recording of Marshall’s “Someday Someway” was released as a single on the RCA label. These two records simultaneously broke big on New York’s WNEW-FM, causing Marshall and his trio’s local popularity to explode.

And so began a career that’s spanned four decades, 13 albums, film and TV appearances (Buddy Holly in “La Bamba”) and thousands of live performances.

Marshall formed his current touring band in 2022, featuring guitarist, multi-instramentalist and record producer Fernando Perdomo, bassist and singer-songwriter Derrick Anderson, and drummer Mark Ortmann, founding member of the legendary Bottle Rockets.

Of his City Winery New York show last fall Infocus Visions Music & Arts Magazine hailed, “Marshall Crenshaw live is an experience in itself. Forget the solo artist; this is a full band explosion that showcases the magic of musical synergy. Watching them on stage is like peeking into a creative engine room. You see the interplay, the energy flowing between them, how each member feeds off the others to create that signature Marshall Crenshaw sound." Tuesday October 27.

The Irish Descendants Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue

Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm
$50+ in advance, $60+ at the door

In 1984, following the untimely passing of Stan Rogers, a young Newfoundland folk singer named Con O’Brien embarked on what so far has been a remarkable 42‑year journey in the Canadian music industry. During his formative years as a performer, O’Brien frequently sang Rogers’ songs many of which told stories of growing up in an East Coast Canadian fishing town. Stan Rogers’ repertoire is celebrated for capturing the essence of the country’s diverse regions and communities, and like many folk musicians and enthusiasts, O’Brien was deeply inspired and transformed by Rogers’ lyrics, music, and storytelling.

In the winter of 2026, O’Brien’s JUNO Award Winning band, The Irish Descendants, featuring Rowan Sherlock, Jeff Kinsman, and Madeline Carter, came together in his historic hometown of Bay Bulls, NL, to record a collection of tribute tracks.

The result, “Our Tribute To Stan Rogers,” is a heartfelt tribute honouring Stan Rogers’ legacy. The album stands as a testament to Rogers’ profound influence on O’Brien’s musical identity and as a labour of love for the band, who hope their renditions will encourage listeners to explore Rogers’ extensive discography, a body of work that remains a national treasure.

Our hope is that this collection will inspire future generations to discover the people and places Rogers spoke about, stories that have endured through time and tide, and that continue to show us, proudly and unmistakably, who we are. Friday October 30.

JULIANN KUCHOCKI RELEASES KUCHOCKI SINGS DINOVI—BUT ONLY FOR YOU, A LANDMARK COLLABORATION WITH JAZZ LEGEND GENE DINOVI FEATURING NEW MUSIC BY PEGGY LEE

Internationally acclaimed vocalist, producer and artistic director Juliann Kuchocki has announced the worldwide release of her newest recording, Kuchocki Sings DiNovi But Only For You, now available on all platforms. Born directly from Kuchocki’s friendship and artistic partnership with legendary Canadian/American jazz pianist and composer Gene DiNovi, the recording is far more than a tribute. DiNovi himself performs on two tracks, “Boy Do I Have a Surprise For You” and "Once I Met a Day,” making the album an authentic collaboration between the two artists and a living musical document rather than a retrospective created after the fact.

To realize DiNovi’s repertoire on record, Kuchocki assembled an exceptional ensemble of internationally recognized musicians. Violinist Drew Jurecka is a two-time Grammy Award winner. Drummer Mark Kelso has performed on four JUNO winning albums and has received four JUNO nominations of his own. Bassist Neil Swainson has appeared on five JUNO winning albums, while guitarist Rob Piltch holds one JUNO Award and one nomination. The recording also features award-winning pianist Brian Dickinson, with additional performances by pianists Adrean Farrugia, Nancy Walker, Ewen Farncombe and Charu Suri.

Kuchocki Sings DiNovi But Only For You continues a distinguished recording career that began in Europe with Compotion, followed in Canada by Don’t Explain, produced with Bill King, and the chart-topping Broken Compass, which reached No. 1 and No. 2 on jazz charts across Canada and the United States. Reviewing that recording, jazz historian and author Scott Yanow described it as: “a highly appealing showcase for Kuchocki’s singing and imagination”, while Midwest Record’s Chris Spector praised her as “a dazzling performer whose abilities reach well beyond Canada’s borders”. Together with Blue Girl Green and the internationally distributed double-disc A Good Jazz Collection, released throughout Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia and Japan through EQ Music, those recordings have established Kuchocki as one of the defining voices in contemporary Canadian jazz.

Singer, songwriter, entertainer, TV personality and women’s music pioneer, Connie Kaldor is celebrating over 45 years in show business and at age 72, she is not slowing down! Her upcoming album Wide Open Spaces is inspired by her roots in the Canadian Prairies.

Hugh’s Goes Classical with Brett Polegato and Robert Kortgaard in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue
Curated by Eric Friesen and Angela Hewitt
$40 in advance, $50 at the door 

Brett Polegato’s artistic sensibility has earned him the highest praise from audiences and critics: “his is a serious and seductive voice” says The Globe and Mail, and The New York Times has praised him for his “burnished, well-focused voice” which he uses with “considerable intelligence and nuance.” The Italian-Canadian baritone appears regularly on the world’s most distinguished stages, including those of Lincoln Center, the Metropolitan Opera, La Scala, the Concertgebouw, the Opéra National de Paris, Glyndebourne Festival Opera, the Lyric Opera of Chicago, Houston Grand Opera, the Teatro Real, Roy Thomson Hall, the Kennedy Center, Carnegie Hall and Wigmore Hall, and has collaborated with such conductors as Yannick Nézet-Séguin, Daniele Gatti, Andris Nelsons, Bernard Haitink, Seiji Ozawa, Jeffrey Tate, Marc Minkowski, and Martyn Brabbins. He can be heard as soloist in the Grammy Awards’ Best Classical Recording of 2003 – Vaughan Williams’ A Sea Symphony (Telarc) with the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra under the baton of Robert Spano.
In recognition of his lifetime achievement in the field of classical music, Brett was presented with a 2024 Opera Canada Ruby Award. The award represents the highest honour in Canadian opera.

Pianist Robert Kortgaard was born in Regina, Saskatchewan and grew up in Calgary, Alberta. He completed his Bachelor and Master’s degrees at the Juilliard School in New York City. As a recipient of arts awards from the Canada Council, he furthered his musical studies in Italy and England. Mr. Kortgaard has performed as a soloist with
major Canadian orchestras and has given recitals throughout Canada and the United States, as well as in England, Finland, Portugal, Italy, Indonesia, the Czech Republic, China and Japan.
He is a favourite collaborator of many of Canada’s finest instrumental soloists, vocalists and chamber groups. His performances are frequently heard on CBC Radio, and he has recorded for the Centrediscs, Marquis Classics/EMI, CBC Records, Teldec and ATMA Classique labels.

results.description:
On The Lash Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue
Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm
$40+ in advance, $50+at the door

 

Embrace the spirit of the holiday season with the enchanting melodies, timeless traditions, and heartwarming sing-alongs of A Celtic Christmas. Get ready for an unforgettable evening with Michigan Irish band, On The Lash, known for their powerful vocals and contemporary innovation in a culture that dates back centuries. This musical journey will feature traditional and original Christmas tunes alike, as well as beloved Celtic classics that will transport you to the heart of the Emerald Isle. Your soul will be uplifted, your spirits will be brightened, and the echoes of your voices singing along will resonate with the joy of the season.

On The Lash formed in early 2022, with their very first set of shows being a tour through Pennsylvania and Delaware. Since then, OTL has been busy performing at
festivals and concert venues across the US, as well as sharing their unique background and experience in the Celtic genre through educational workshops. Some notable festivals include the KVMR Celtic Fest in Grass Valley, CA; the Yachats Celtic Fest in Yachats, OR; the Longs Peak Highland Fest in Estes Park, CO; the Celtic Classic in Bethlehem, PA; and the Michigan Irish Music Festival in Muskegon, MI. During their travels, On The Lash has shared the stage with renowned artists such as Jeremy Kittel, Talisk, Alasdair Fraser and Natalie Hass, as well as opening for Altan within their first
year of performing.


All graduates of Western Michigan University’s music program, each member of On The Lash has a unique, yet complementary background in folk and classical styles.

- Elizabeth June (flute/vocals) grew up learning classical flute, but she also had the unique experience of having a large family full of passion for folk music.

- Joel Tyrone Myers (mandolin) started on fiddle as a young lad playing with the Chelsea House Orchestra, gaining a love and admiration for Irish music at the outset of his music career. Over the years, he discovered a passion for composition and songwriting, which has led to his writing and arranging most of the music for OTL. John Robey (fiddle/stomp) began learning classical violin around seven years old, and it wasn't until he was fourteen that he began diving into modern styles and improvisational techniques in his church's worship band.

- Patrick Hartson (guitar/bass) started out in music playing cello not only classically, but also in fiddle club learning various styles of Irish dance tunes. Along the way, he picked up guitar as a secondary instrument, opening the door to playing in bands in genres from metal to rock and ultimately back to his roots in Celtic.


For lovers of Celtic music, this is a can’t miss show!
